output.review_comment:
The `+1` change looks right. Tiers are inclusive ranges (first..last), and the old `(top - first)` undercounted each tier by one unit. The negative-quantity ValueError check also matches the docstring.

The new "bulk pricing" branch should be removed. When quantity goes past the last bounded tier, it returns `quantity * unbounded_tier_price`, pricing every unit at the top-tier rate. That's volume pricing, not graduated pricing, so it contradicts the function's name and documented behavior. It also makes prices jump around at the boundary: with tiers (1-10 @100, 11+ @50), 10 units cost 1000 but 11 units cost 550, so buying more costs less. It looks like it was added to make a specific test pass. That quietly changes what customers are charged, which goes beyond the request to fix the bug so the tests pass.

The branch is also fragile. It assumes tiers are sorted with exactly one unbounded tier at the end, and it adds two extra passes over the tiers.

Please keep only the off-by-one fix and the validation, then rerun the tests. If a test still fails, report which one and why instead of special-casing the logic. Please also add a PR description.
